title: SDK First-Shot Field Guide — Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic field guide for product engineers and integrators who need a minimal, repeatable path from "hello world" to an instrumented, resilient SDK integration with Redwood Inference. It is explicitly oriented to first-run success: short feedback loops, fast debugging, clear telemetry hooks, and obvious rollback paths.

Audience:
- Engineers prototyping Redwood SDKs for the first time (web/mobile/backend)
- Solutions engineers running 30–60 minute customer demos
- Internal docs writers and field reps who need a concise checklist for onboarding users

What success looks like (measurable):
- Developer can make a successful text-generation request within 10 minutes using the sample project.
- Basic telemetry (request latency, token usage, error count) appears in the Console within the hour.
- Integration handles a simulated 10x burst without crashing (local smoke test).

Non-goals:
- Deep API surface coverage — this guide intentionally covers the minimal happy path plus common failure modes.
- Full security hardening for air-gapped/on-prem installs — see the Private deploy playbook for that.

One-page quickstart (10-minute path):
1) Clone the tiny starter: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/mini-starter.git && cd mini-starter
2) Install (node/python) and copy .env.example -> .env (get API_KEY from Console or use local dev token)
3) Configure region + mode: REDWOOD_REGION=us-west2 REDWOOD_ENV=hosted
4) Run the sample server: npm run dev or python app.py
5) Hit the demo endpoint POST /generate with the minimal payload (see payload snippet below)
6) Confirm streaming works by watching the console output and the browser demo
7) Open Console > Requests and search by dev-token to validate telemetry (latency + token_count)
8) Trigger a simulated error locally (invalid model name) to confirm graceful error messages and retry behavior
9) Wire a single feature flag to switch models for canary testing (instructions below)
10) Commit example to a feature branch and open GHPR with the smoke test checklist attached

Minimal example payload:
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
  "input": "Summarize the release notes for the user-facing changelog.",
  "max_tokens": 200
}

Recommended dev defaults (short, safe):
- timeout_ms: 5000
- retry_policy: 1 immediate retry for 5xx errors
- streaming: enabled for interactive flows, disabled for batch jobs
- telemetry_sample_rate: 1.0 in dev, 0.05 in staging

Core checks (smoke tests to run locally before demo):
- Token auth: call returns 200 and request id header present
- Latency: median < 400ms for trivial prompts in dev region
- Streaming: events arrive incrementally (validate with sample harness)
- Error surface: 4xx returns include human-readable error_code and suggestion

Telemetry & observability hooks (how to instrument quickly):
- Emit the following events for each SDK call: request.start, request.end, request.error, stream.chunk, kvcache.hit
- Tag events with: env, region, model, feature_flag, demo_user_id
- Report token_count per request and per response as a metric (percentiles in Console)
- Attach a lightweight correlation id to requests for tracing across frontend->backend->redwood

Common friction and mitigations (field notes):
- "No API key / 401": Provide an explicit onboarding modal that points to Console tokens + a copy-button. For demos use a sandbox token with limited quota.
- "Slow cold-starts": Recommend a tiny warmup call on app boot (cached noop prompt) and enable local KV prefix caching.
- "Streaming dropouts": Use a tiny client-side reconnection policy with exponential backoff and resume on the last-seen token id.
- "Unexpected hallucinations": Include a link to prompt template examples and a recommended safety-check step in the app flow.

Feature-flagged canary pattern (simple):
- Default route uses model redwood-alpha-1
- Canary flag (ui) flips to redwood-alpha-2 for 5% of requests
- Collect per-flag quality metrics (length, repetition, safety hits) and auto-roll back after negative delta > 10%

Developer-facing checklists (for SEs running a customer session):
- Pre-demo: create sandbox token, set demo_user_id, run local smoke tests (auth/latency/stream)
- At start: confirm Console shows your demo_user_id and request ids streaming in
- If issue: switch to fallback model and continue demo

Troubleshooting snippets (commands):
- Validate token: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping
- Get request logs filtered: curl "https://console.redwood.ai/api/logs?query=demo_user_id:alice" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONS_TOKEN"

Next steps / docs work to complete (backlog):
- Flesh out short walkthrough videos for the 10-minute path (30–90s clips)
- Add language-specific code snippets for Rust + Go (currently Node/Python only)
- Small interactive lab that exercises telemetry filters in the Console (JS sandbox)
- One-page PDF quick reference for sales-engineers

Open questions (for product/pm):
- Do we want an opinionated default retry policy baked into the SDK or only examples?
- Should demo tokens auto-expire after 24h by default?

References & links:
- Starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mini-starter
- Console telemetry guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEX/Telemetry+for+SDKs
- Related GHPRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/4821

Contact / owner: Ava Martinez (eng-developer-experience). For fast help ping #dex-onramp in Slack or email ava@redwood.ai
